text: Outlaw Run is a wooden roller coaster located at Silver Dollar City in Branson, Missouri, designed by Alan Schilke and manufactured by Rocky Mountain Construction (RMC), making it RMC's first wooden roller coaster. It became the first wooden roller coaster to feature multiple inversions and has a 162-foot (49 m) drop at an 81-degree angle, which is the fourth steepest and fourth tallest among wooden roller coasters. The ride reaches a maximum speed of 68 mph (109 km/h), placing it as the sixth-fastest wooden coaster in the world, and it includes three inversions, one of which is a double heartline roll. Outlaw Run is tied with Wildfire at Kolmården Wildlife Park, also built by RMC, for the most inversions on a wooden coaster. Development of the concept began in 2009, with planning for a new 2013 attraction initiated by Herschend Family Entertainment, who sought a "world first" ride with marketing appeal, including a double barrel roll. Joel Manby, CEO of Herschend, wanted a wooden coaster with a unique element, and after Rocky Mountain Construction demonstrated their steel coaster, New Texas Giant, in 2011, the contract was secured. Marketing began in 2011 at the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions trade show, with a teaser website launched during construction that revealed a Western stagecoach theme and an announcement date of August 9, 2012. On that date, Silver Dollar City officially announced Outlaw Run would open in the second quarter of 2013. The ride opened to a limited audience on March 13, 2013, with a public opening two days later, and official celebrations occurred in April. At a cost of $10 million, it was the most expensive attraction at Silver Dollar City in over a decade. The 2,937-foot-long (895 m) ride uses laminated wood with a steel plate called Topper Track in the upper layers, a technology developed by RMC to reduce maintenance and improve ride smoothness. The track features twisted wooden beams developed over four years, enabling dynamic elements. Each train holds twelve pairs of riders, with riders needing to be at least 48 inches (122 cm) tall and secured in fiberglass seats with a U-shaped lap bar; the ride uses steel wheels instead of polyurethane. The ride's theme centers on stagecoaches and the Wild West, with a storyline where outlaws attempt to rob stagecoaches, and the "good guys" always win. The ride begins with a chain lift hill, a small pre-drop, and a 162-foot (49 m) 81-degree drop, followed by an outside banked turn, a 100-foot (30 m) double down, a 70-foot (21 m) double up, a twist and turn, a wave turn, a high-speed float, and two heartline rolls before returning to the station. A single ride cycle takes about 1 minute and 27 seconds. Outlaw Run debuted with the steepest drop on any wooden roller coaster at the time, though it no longer claims to be the only wooden coaster with inversions due to the opening of Hades 360, which also features inversions. It is also the fifth-fastest wooden coaster in the world, with a top speed of 68 mph (109 km/h), though this record was later surpassed by Goliath at Six Flags Great America in 2014. Outlaw Run retains the record for the wooden roller coaster with the most inversions. The ride received favorable reviews, with Arthur Levine of About.com praising its layout, Brady MacDonald of the Los Angeles Times including it in his top 13 most anticipated 2013 attractions, and Marcus Leshock, Brandy McDonnell, and Tim Baldwin offering positive feedback. In its debut year, Outlaw Run won the Golden Ticket Award for Best New Ride with 45% of the vote and ranked as the seventh-best wooden roller coaster worldwide.
